summary: Sequoia National Forest lookout active since before 1916, staffed yearly until 1992, now used only in extreme fire danger; current tower's origin is disputed across sources.

facts.status_note: staffed only intermittently, during periods of very high fire danger or when volunteer lookouts are available, rather than continuously

access.note: open to the public only when staffed, via the Buck Rock Foundation volunteer lookout program

visit.trail_note: located in the Hume Lake Ranger District; not described as drive-up in available sources

evidence.supports: detection site since 1916; 1924 tower used until 1959; present 40-foot tower moved in 1967
evidence.quote: Delilah Lookout on the Sequoia National Forest has been a detection site since 1916. In 1924 a tower with a ground residence went into service until 1959. The present 40' metal tower with live-in cab was moved to the site in 1967 from Lenore Naval Air Base.

evidence.supports: pre-1916 original lookout, 1924 tower with cabin replaced in 1959, 1937 CCC tower, 1960 Lemoore tower, NHLR registration June 10 2001, staffed yearly until 1992
evidence.quote: The original lookout was built pre 1916 with the tower built in 1924 with a cabin below and replaced in 1959 and in 1967 with a steel tower from Lemore Naval Air Force Base.

evidence.supports: 1937 CCC 50-foot tower, 1960 70-foot Lemoore tower, staffed yearly until 1992, intermittent staffing since
evidence.quote: It has seen several incarnations including a 50 foot metal tower with live-in cab constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1937. In 1960 this structure was replaced with a 70 foot tall metal tower from Lemoore Navel Air Station. The lookout was staffed yearly, funded by both the California Department of Forestry and the Sequoia National Forest Service until 1992.

evidence.supports: 1930 two-room house built, 1943 telephone line rebuild, c.1959 65-foot Army surplus tower, 1961 White Deer Fire evacuation
evidence.quote: September 18, 1930: "A two room house, for living quarters, has been built at the Delilah lookout station, north of Dunlap, Fresno county." ... November 14, 1943: "Workmen started last Monday to rebuild 3 miles of the Delilah fire lookout telephone line destroyed in the Goat Corral fire of September..." ... c.1959: ( The date is a guess ) A 65-foot steel Army surplus steel tower with a 15 x 15 foot flat roof cab was moved from a U.S. Army training camp to this site.

The lookout was evacuated Sunday by Mrs. Fern Billings after the fire erupted in two spots in White Deer Canyon north of state highway 180. She was replaced by Bob Sparks who was evacuated Monday when flames flashed by the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three sources disagree on the current steel tower's height, origin base, and installation year: NHLR says 40-foot tower from 'Lenore Naval Air Base' in 1967; fire-lookouts.org says a 1937 CCC 50-foot tower was replaced in 1960 by a 70-foot tower from Lemoore Naval Air Station; californialookouts.weebly.com says a 65-foot Army-surplus tower from a U.S. Army training camp arrived c.1959 (noting the date is a guess). All three agree the tower is ex-military/government surplus steel, but no two agree on height, year, or exact source installation. Reported in the story as an unresolved disagreement rather than picking one.

sources.title: Delilah Fire Lookout, U.S.F.S., Sequoia National Forest Lookout

notes_for_editor: Significant three-way disagreement on the current tower's height/origin/install year across all three sources used; flagged in both the story and resolved_conflicts rather than silently picking one. Brief's access was 'public'; narrowed to 'restricted' with a note since sources say it's only open to the public when staffed (intermittently, via volunteers). Did not independently verify the Buck Rock Foundation's current program status beyond what fire-lookouts.org states. The 1930 two-room house and 1943 telephone-line rebuild sentences were confirmed live on californialookouts.weebly.com but had no evidence entry in this file; added 1930/1943 events and folded their quotes into the existing cite-3 evidence entry.
